subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: Should Codex computer watchdog budgeting continue accepting plain decimal duration strings, and does that grammar exactly match the computer executor’s runtime parsing?
rationale: The patch deliberately narrows previously accepted inputs, but the available evidence proves only the watchdog resolver and generic Codex JSON transport—not the complete computer execution path that determines how long the action actually runs.

options.title: Align and prove the grammar
options.body: Trace the computer schema and executor, then adjust or document the parser so execution duration and watchdog duration use one identical contract.

options.title: Accept the current narrowing
options.body: Confirm that decimal strings are intentionally supported, non-decimal strings are invalid, and the executor cannot run longer than the revised watchdog budget for rejected inputs.

recommendation.title: Align and prove the grammar
recommendation.body: Trace the computer schema and executor, then adjust or document the parser so execution duration and watchdog duration use one identical contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from recent Codex app-server and dynamic-tool lifecycle work.
